q: A process of making a magnetic material into a magnet is called _____.
e: A process of making a magnetic material into a magnet is called magnetisation. Every magnet has a north pole and a south pole, and like poles push apart involving material.

q: Two types of magnetisation are magnetisation by stroking and magnetisation using _____.
e: Two types of magnetisation are magnetisation by stroking and magnetisation using direct current. Direct current here means the flow of electric charge. Alternating current: the flow of electric charge.

q: The best way to make powerful magnets is to use the magnetic effect of an _____.
e: The best way to make powerful magnets is to use the magnetic effect of an electric current. Electric current here means the flow of electric charge. Electric field: the influence around electric charge, not the field of a magnet.

q: A steel bar placed inside a solenoid with direct current passed through it becomes a _____.
e: A steel bar placed inside a solenoid with direct current passed through it becomes a permanent magnet. Permanent magnet here means a body that attracts iron and has two poles. Temporary magnet: a body that attracts iron and has two poles.

q: If an iron bar is placed inside a solenoid with direct current, it becomes magnetised temporarily as a(n) _____.
e: If an iron bar is placed inside a solenoid with direct current, it becomes magnetised temporarily as a(n) electromagnet. The physics in this sentence is built around electromagnet. Permanent magnet: a body that attracts iron and has two poles.

q: The polarities of the magnet produced by a solenoid depend on the _____ of the electric current.
e: The polarities of the magnet produced by a solenoid depend on the direction of the electric current. Current is charge passing a point per second.

q: In magnetisation by stroking, the magnet must be lifted _____ above the bar between successive strokes.
e: In magnetisation by stroking, the magnet must be lifted high above the bar between successive strokes. Every magnet has a north pole and a south pole, and like poles push apart.

q: The end of the steel bar where the strokes finish always has the _____ polarity to that of the end of the stroking magnet in contact with it.
e: The end of the steel bar where the strokes finish always has the opposite polarity to that of the end of the stroking magnet in contact with it. Every magnet has a north pole and a south pole, and like poles push apart. Same: lined up together, which is how a bar becomes magnetised.

q: When a piece of unmagnetised magnetic material is brought near to the pole of a permanent magnet, it is attracted and becomes a magnet itself. This is called _____.
e: When a piece of unmagnetised magnetic material is brought near to the pole of a permanent magnet, it is attracted and becomes a magnet itself. This is called induced magnetism. Every magnet has a north pole and a south pole, and like poles push apart.

q: In induced magnetism, the north pole of the permanent magnet induces a(n) _____ in the near end of the soft iron.
e: In induced magnetism, the north pole of the permanent magnet induces a(n) $S$-pole in the near end of the soft iron. Every magnet has a north pole and a south pole, and like poles push apart.

q: In induced magnetism, the far end of the soft iron becomes a(n) _____.
e: In induced magnetism, the far end of the soft iron becomes a(n) $N$-pole. The physics in this sentence is built around $N$-pole.
